# Project Governance 2.8.1

Runtime bootstrap and startup candidate installation now require the complete Python dependency
closure pinned by version and approved wheel hashes inside the verified Governance wheel. Missing
or altered dependencies fail installation instead of resolving an unreviewed set. Release proof
compares clean installations and exercises the bootstrapped environment.

Adopters must deliberately update their runtime lock, refresh the bootstrap launcher from this
release, and rerun bootstrap before relying on this installation guarantee. Follow the [agent upgrade sequence](https://github.com/copper-labs/project-governance/blob/2.8.1/docs/guides/user-guide.md#adopt-dependency-locking-from-281), including its first-install limitation and strict-CI alternative. Older launchers do not
acquire hash enforcement merely by installing a newer runtime. Startup compatibility remains marked
as requiring deliberate integration. Hosts need a compatible published wheel for each dependency;
source-distribution builds are not allowed. Python and installer tooling are outside this runtime
dependency lock.

Shared guidance now defines focused adoption proof for stage routing, lane deadlines, and early
commit-message validation, with a small comparison using existing telemetry. No telemetry collector,
schema, automatic alert, or additional validation gate is introduced. Provider instruction routing
also consistently includes the Gemini adapter.
